## Natural history notes

A large pale green silk moth characterized by long sweeping hindwing tails, eyespots on all four wings, and a white fuzzy body. In Florida, the Luna Moth is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, mixed woods, parks, wooded neighborhoods, and forest edges where host trees such as sweetgum, hickory, walnut, persimmon, and other hardwoods occur. Adults are nocturnal and do not feed, living only long enough to mate and lay eggs, while the large green caterpillars feed on tree leaves and eventually spin papery cocoons in leaf litter or among leaves.
